notes: **Presenter:** Mark. One person, one list, in video order.
**Before recording anything:** Mark has a Qube login in Chrome on his own laptop. Everything is typed into Qube itself. Close anything that shows an email, account name, API key or notification.
**Shoot order:** A6 → A7 → A8 (the Qube run, first, because it decides line 13) → A9 (13A only) → A10 → A0 talking takes. The editor builds A1–A5 and A11 in parallel.

open.text: **Line 13 depends on your run.** Do A6–A8 before filming the talking takes; 13A if it made money, 13B if it lost money. Both are written, nothing to fill in.
**A9:** if your Qube login has no simulation-account screen, A9 is the graphic.
**M15 also opens on "Grok… killed day trading"** (brief flag): give the two videos different first frames. M14's is the "KILLED?" stamp on a falling chart.

rows.how: **Read fast, about 3 words a second, no pauses between lines. Aim for about 52s (13B about 49s).** 1. Laptop camera or phone vertical (9:16), eye level, office lights on, lock focus and exposure. Leave room above the head for the top third. 2. Do the A6–A8 run first and pick line 13 (A8 step 5). 3. Record the hook 3 times: "Grok might have just killed day trading forever." 4. Record lines 1–15 in one take, with only the line 13 you picked. 2 full takes. 5. **Close-up**, phone moved in so the face fills the frame, 3 takes: "Sounds careful, right? Here's what scares me." 6. **CTA**, 3 takes: "Comment QUBE and I'll send you the link for the free sign-up." **CHECK: the take you send is under 60s. If it runs over, re-record faster; don't cut a line.**

rows.how: 1. Chrome, full screen, zoom 125%, no tabs or bookmarks showing. Log in to Qube. 2. Start screen recording (QuickTime → New Screen Recording, whole screen). 3. Start a new strategy by describing it in plain English. 4. Type by hand (don't paste), exactly: `Buy Tesla any day it jumps 4% or more. Sell at a 6% gain or 3% loss.` 5. Send it, and keep recording until Qube has written the strategy. Hold 2s on it. 6. If Qube asks for the starting amount or the test dates, set `$10,000` and the longest period it offers (up to five years), one trade at a time. **CHECK: Qube's strategy must read: buy Tesla after a day it's up 4% or more, sell at +6% or −3% from the buy price. If it reads it differently, type it once more as `Buy Tesla at the close on any day it closes up 4% or more. Sell when it's 6% above my buy price or 3% below it.` and use that. Never change the 4%, 6% or 3%.** 7. Screenshot the typed sentence (typed.png).
rows.what: Typing the Tesla trade into Qube

rows.how: 1. Same recording or a new one. 2. Run the backtest on the strategy from A6. 3. Keep recording until the result appears. Hold 3s. 4. Open the list of every trade. Scroll top to bottom in about 3s, then stop where at least 3 red losing trades are on screen together. Hold 3s. 5. Screenshot that spot (trades.png). **CHECK: whatever Qube shows is the result. Don't re-run or tweak the strategy to get a better number, and never change a number.** **CHECK: the trade list must show the losing trades in red.**

1. Screenshot the result summary (result.png). 2. **CHECK: result.png must show the start value, the end value, the gain or loss, the test dates, the number of trades and the worst drop. If one is missing, open the screen that shows it and screenshot that too.** 3. Write those six numbers in a note exactly as Qube shows them. 4. Send result.png and the note to the editor. 5. **Pick line 13: end value above the start value → say 13A ("It made money, losses and all. Next, it goes on a simulation account."). End value below the start value → say 13B ("It lost money.").** 6. Editor: on-screen result line from the note: main line `start value → end value · gain or loss` (Inter Bold 44px, a gain in green #22C55E, a loss in red #EF4444); small line `Backtest, not live results · test dates · number of trades · worst drop` (Inter Bold 26px, light grey #9AA3AE). **CHECK: every number in the text is on result.png. If they don't match, stop and tell Mark.**

Only if line 13 is 13A. 1. In Qube, open the same strategy and record the screen where you'd run it on a simulation account. Hold 3s. The editor adds on-screen text `Simulation account · fake money` over it. 2. If Qube has no such screen on your login, tell the editor to use a graphic instead: Canva 1080×640, three grey #2A2F37 boxes left to right `PAST PRICES` → `SIMULATION ACCOUNT · fake money` → `LIVE`, the middle one gold #E8B04B. **CHECK: no live account, balance or broker name on screen.**

Chrome, full screen, zoom 125%, logged out (a private window works). Open https://www.tqx.ai/igqube2 and scroll slowly to "Start free" and "Free · no card required". 5s. **CHECK: the page's sample backtest (+55.43%, 814 trades, Sharpe 1.22) must not be in the shot.**
Full screen 1080×1920, #0B0F14, "Comment QUBE" centred, Instrument Serif 88px white, "QUBE" in gold #E8B04B. 2s.

lines.text: Grok might have just killed day trading forever.
See, people are putting six Grok bots into one group chat, letting them trade, and they say it's making them thousands.
One guy said he turned $87 into $8,000, and another one claims he turned $90 into $14,000.
And no single bot does it alone, so let me break down exactly how it works.
Grok lets you set up six bots in one group chat.
The first one is the scout, which watches the markets for any big moves.
The second one is the news bot, it finds exactly why it's moving according to the news.
And then we have the chart bot, which picks the entry, the exit, and the stop.
But this is the one that matters the most.
It's called the skeptic.
Its whole job is to argue against every single trade.
It tells the desk to buy, wait, or skip.
So no bad idea gets past it before any money moves.
And the best part of this is that it runs on its own cloud computer 24-7, so you can run this exact setup without lifting a finger.
If you want to learn how to set this up, comment the word Grok and I'll send it right over to you.
